## Related

<h3 id="toml-token-kind"><code>TomlTokenKind</code></h3>

```rux
pub enum TomlTokenKind: int32 {
    End = 0,
    BareKey = 1,
    Text = 2,
    Integer = 3,
    Float = 4,
    Boolean = 5,
    DateTime = 6,
    Equals = 7,
    Dot = 8,
    Comma = 9,
    LeftBracket = 10,
    RightBracket = 11,
    LeftBrace = 12,
    RightBrace = 13,
    Newline = 14,
    Error = 15
}
```

What kind of token this is.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Toml/Src/Lexer.rux#L15)

**Cases**

| Name           | Value | Description                                                                                    |
| -------------- | ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `End`          | `0`   | The input is exhausted.                                                                        |
| `BareKey`      | `1`   | A bare key: letters, digits, underscores and hyphens.                                          |
| `Text`         | `2`   | A quoted key or a string value; the span excludes the quotes and the text may need unescaping. |
| `Integer`      | `3`   | An integer, in any of the four bases.                                                          |
| `Float`        | `4`   | A float, including the infinities and NaN that TOML — unlike JSON — can spell.                 |
| `Boolean`      | `5`   | `true` or `false`.                                                                             |
| `DateTime`     | `6`   | An offset date-time, a local date-time, a local date, or a local time.                         |
| `Equals`       | `7`   | `=`                                                                                            |
| `Dot`          | `8`   | `.`                                                                                            |
| `Comma`        | `9`   | `,`                                                                                            |
| `LeftBracket`  | `10`  | `[`                                                                                            |
| `RightBracket` | `11`  | `]`                                                                                            |
| `LeftBrace`    | `12`  | `{`                                                                                            |
| `RightBrace`   | `13`  | `}`                                                                                            |
| `Newline`      | `14`  | One or more newlines, which TOML treats as significant.                                        |
| `Error`        | `15`  | Something that is not TOML.                                                                    |

<h3 id="toml-text-form"><code>TomlTextForm</code></h3>

```rux
pub enum TomlTextForm: int32 {
    NotText = 0,
    Basic = 1,
    MultiLineBasic = 2,
    Literal = 3,
    MultiLineLiteral = 4,
    Bare = 5
}
```

Which of the four string forms a text token was written in.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Toml/Src/Lexer.rux#L52)

**Cases**

| Name               | Value | Description                                                                                                  |
| ------------------ | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `NotText`          | `0`   | Not a text token.                                                                                            |
| `Basic`            | `1`   | A basic string: escapes honoured, no raw newlines.                                                           |
| `MultiLineBasic`   | `2`   | A multi-line basic string: escapes honoured, newlines allowed, a leading newline trimmed.                    |
| `Literal`          | `3`   | A literal string: no escapes at all, which is what makes it right for Windows paths and regular expressions. |
| `MultiLineLiteral` | `4`   | A multi-line literal string: no escapes, newlines allowed.                                                   |
| `Bare`             | `5`   | A bare key, which has no quotes and no escapes.                                                              |

<h3 id="toml-lex-error"><code>TomlLexError</code></h3>

```rux
pub enum TomlLexError: int32 {
    None = 0,
    UnexpectedByte = 1,
    UnterminatedText = 2,
    BadEscape = 3,
    BadUnicodeEscape = 4,
    MalformedNumber = 5,
    NewlineInText = 6,
    UnescapedControl = 7,
    MalformedDateTime = 8
}
```

Why lexing stopped.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Toml/Src/Lexer.rux#L70)

**Cases**

| Name                | Value | Description                                                                        |
| ------------------- | ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `None`              | `0`   | Nothing went wrong.                                                                |
| `UnexpectedByte`    | `1`   | A byte that begins no token.                                                       |
| `UnterminatedText`  | `2`   | A string the input ended before closing.                                           |
| `BadEscape`         | `3`   | An escape sequence TOML does not define.                                           |
| `BadUnicodeEscape`  | `4`   | A unicode escape that is not the right number of digits, or names no scalar value. |
| `MalformedNumber`   | `5`   | A number whose shape TOML grammar does not allow.                                  |
| `NewlineInText`     | `6`   | A raw newline inside a single-line string.                                         |
| `UnescapedControl`  | `7`   | A control character appearing unescaped where TOML forbids it.                     |
| `MalformedDateTime` | `8`   | A date or time that is not the shape RFC 3339 defines.                             |

<h3 id="toml-decode-text"><code>TomlDecodeText</code></h3>

```rux
pub func TomlDecodeText(
    allocator: Allocator,
    span: char8[..],
    form: TomlTextForm,
    bad: *var bool
) -> String ! TextError
```

Decodes a text token's span into an owned string, honouring the escapes its form allows.
A literal string is copied unchanged — that is what makes it the right form for a Windows path — while a
basic string has its escapes resolved, including the line-ending backslash that lets a multi-line string be
wrapped in the source without the wrapping appearing in the value.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Toml/Src/Lexer.rux#L509)

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type           | Description                                                     |
| ----------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `allocator` | `Allocator`    | where the storage comes from                                    |
| `span`      | `char8[..]`    | the raw text the token covers                                   |
| `form`      | `TomlTextForm` | which quoting form the text was written in                      |
| `bad`       | `*var bool`    | receives the offset of the first byte that could not be decoded |

**Returns**: the decoded text, or why it could not be stored
